avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone secretion, decreasing potassium excretion and increasing serum potassium levels; concurrent supplementation increases hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; monitor serum potassium closely if patient has renal impairment; counsel on dietary potassium restriction

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen, indomethacin)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow and inhibit prostaglandin-mediated vasodilation; combined effect increases risk of acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, use lowest dose for shortest duration and monitor renal function and potassium

caution_supplements.name: Licorice root
caution_supplements.mechanism: Licorice causes sodium retention and potassium depletion, potentially reducing fosinopril efficacy and causing electrolyte imbalance
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure and electrolytes; limit licorice consumption or consider alternative supplements

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild sympathomimetic effects that could reduce antihypertensive efficacy of fosinopril
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure response; counsel on potential interaction

avoid_foods.name: High-potassium foods (bananas, spinach, sweet potatoes, tomatoes, coconut water)
avoid_foods.mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce potassium excretion; excessive dietary potassium intake increases risk of hyperkalemia, especially with renal dysfunction
avoid_foods.action: Counsel on dietary potassium restriction; obtain baseline potassium levels and monitor periodically

caution_foods.name: Sodium-containing foods and salt substitutes containing potassium
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium may blunt antihypertensive effects; potassium-based salt substitutes increase hyperkalemia risk
caution_foods.action: Recommend DASH diet and sodium restriction (<2.3g daily); advise against potassium-containing salt substitutes

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum potassium, creatinine, and blood pressure regularly, particularly within 1-2 weeks of initiation and dose adjustment. Counsel patients on signs of hyperkalemia (weakness, palpitations) and acute kidney injury (reduced urine output, fatigue).
